 Petrol and diesel prices could drop ahead of South Africa’s December holidays
 --> 
 Posted on 21 November 2026 
 By Zayaan Marthinus 
 Tags: Central Energy Fund , December 2026 fuel prices , December fuel prices , December holidays , diesel price forecast , diesel prices , festive season travel , fuel levy , fuel price forecast , motoring , petrol price forecast , petrol prices , road trips , South Africa fuel prices , South African motorists 
 December fuel prices could fall in South Africa, giving motorists some breathing room in their festive road trip budgets. The latest Central Energy Fund figures point to lower prices for both petrol and diesel, with the final adjustments still to be confirmed.
 Engin Akyurt / Pexels / Illustrative purposes only
 According to BusinessTech’s latest report , petrol and diesel prices have made a ‘complete U-turn’, moving into over-recovery territory despite the partial reversal of the government’s temporary fuel-tax relief in December.
 Data from the Central Energy Fund (CEF) at the end of the third week of November shows an over-recovery of R3.44 per litre for 93 petrol and R3.68 for 95 petrol. Diesel is showing over-recoveries of R1.58 for 0.05% diesel and R2.00 for 0.005% diesel.
 The current projections point to a possible R3.44/l cut for 93 petrol and R3.68/l for 95 petrol, while diesel could fall by between R1.58/l and R2/l before other monthly adjustments are taken into account.
 BusinessTech cautioned that the CEF figures are not final, as they do not include factors such as the slate levy and other monthly adjustments.
 Under-recoveries
 The projected cuts come despite Treasury beginning to unwind its temporary fuel-price intervention. From December, 50 cents per litre will be added back to the petrol levy and R1.50/l to diesel, with the remaining relief scheduled to fall away in January.
 The developments mark a sharp turnaround from earlier forecasts.
 BusinessTech previously reported that petrol and diesel were facing under-recoveries in October, with petrol showing a shortfall of up to R1.38/l. The temporary fuel-levy cuts announced by Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana were expected to prevent significant increases.
 The government subsequently cut petrol prices by just 1c/l in November, while diesel prices fell by more than R1/l. The Department of Mineral and Petroleum Resources said the November adjustment was influenced by higher international oil and petroleum-product prices, a weaker rand and a higher slate levy.
 Reuters reported at the time that diesel would fall while petrol would remain ‘little changed’ following the fuel-tax cuts.
 Oil prices drive turnaround
 The latest improvement has largely been driven by a sharp decline in international oil prices.
 BusinessTech reported that oil had fallen to around $91 a barrel, after trading above $100 for much of the previous month and reaching about $118 earlier in November. The lower oil price has significantly improved South Africa’s fuel-price recovery position.
 TopAuto similarly reported that petrol was on track for a cut of about R3/l, describing December as a potential major relief for motorists.
 However, the rand remains a potential risk. BusinessTech said currency movements had offset some of the benefit from cheaper oil, although the impact was currently not large enough to wipe out the fuel-price over-recovery.
 For motorists, the December adjustment could therefore provide some of the most significant relief at the pumps this year, although the final prices will only be confirmed by the Department of Mineral and Petroleum Resources at the beginning of December.
